main_issue: Whether Agent D can keep singing at about 4:45 a.m. in their room daily for four weeks despite the thin walls waking the others, or must change time, place or volume.

A-B.evidence: B backs A's living-room idea (12), offers help carrying (17), proposes earplugs (19), then agrees with A that they may not be enough (23).

A-C.evidence: C says even quiet singing will wake them (7) and that it's every weekday (26); A says the noise is too early on Monday (24). Both are against D's plan, but C's concern is broader than A's Monday-only request.

A-D.evidence: D offers only no bell and quiet singing (8, 10, 15); A says quiet isn't enough (9, 14) and 'we're stuck' (16). D rejects the living room (13).

B-C.evidence: B proposes earplugs for A and B (19). C replies that earplugs might work but would be needed every morning (20). C stays opposed to D's plan, but wants more than B's targeted fixes.

B-D.evidence: B asks for quiet singing (6), moving to the living room (12) and help carrying (17); D refuses each one (13, 18).

C-D.evidence: C says any singing will wake them (7); D says the singing is required and only the bell is dropped (8); C says it's every weekday (26).
